reason: The hypothesis relies on the premise that ML can predict HEA phases and that such prediction enables stability optimization, but the cited evidence only shows ML phase prediction from binary data (E4) and general ML requirements (E1, E2); no evidence supports the claim that ML-optimized composition/processing improves stability across 473–1923 K, nor that phase prediction alone mediates stability. E3 is too vague to support any specific premise.
premises: Machine learning can predict phases of multi-element alloys from binary data
Machine learning models require large, consistent datasets for training
Optimizing composition and processing conditions improves stability of HEAs
Phase prediction is a prerequisite for finding functional HEA materials
Machine learning-based phase prediction has been successfully applied to structural phases
